periods.summary: Sāmoan tatau carries a history spanning three millennia, while tattooing across Oceania developed as distinct living systems of genealogy, rank, protection, service, and belonging. Tā moko, tatau, and other Pacific traditions are not interchangeable motifs.

periods.title: The Japanese body as a field
periods.summary: Large, flowing Japanese compositions grew in conversation with popular visual culture, especially the narrative drama and bold movement of ukiyo-e. Body placement became part of the image’s grammar.

periods.title: Electric speed changes the craft
periods.summary: Samuel O’Reilly patented an electric tattooing machine in New York. Faster repetition helped reshape studio practice, while hand methods continued as skilled traditions in many communities.

periods.title: Subculture becomes a global medium
periods.summary: Maritime flash, circus culture, Chicano fine-line, Japanese revival, punk, queer self-fashioning, fine art, and digital aesthetics expanded tattooing into a global medium with local histories.

anthropologyLenses.title: Identity & belonging
anthropologyLenses.description: Skin can record kinship, status, community, profession, resistance, or chosen family. Meaning is made through relationships, not shape alone.

anthropologyLenses.title: Ritual & protection
anthropologyLenses.description: Pain, endurance, healing, prayer, and transformation may be part of the work. A tattoo can be an event as much as an image.

anthropologyLenses.title: Power & stigma
anthropologyLenses.description: The same mark can signal prestige in one setting and punishment or exclusion in another. Institutions have repeatedly controlled who may mark the body.

anthropologyLenses.title: Memory & self-authorship
anthropologyLenses.description: Contemporary tattoos often hold grief, survival, pleasure, transition, and authorship of the body — meanings with deep historical echoes.

articles.title: From Sailor Flash to Neo-Traditional
articles.paperTitle: From Sailor Flash to Neo-Traditional: The Genealogy of Western Traditional Tattooing
articles.dek: How maritime folk marks became a codified American idiom — then split into faithful revival and illustrative reinvention.
articles.curatorNote: This is where the bold line learned to hold. Read it to feel why a swallow still means coming home.

articles.title: Skin as Image: Realism to Surreal Transformation
articles.paperTitle: Skin as Image: Realism, Portraiture, Miniaturization, Hyperrealism, and Surreal Transformation
articles.dek: Photography, portraiture, and impossible depth pressed into living dermis — and how micro-detail ages.
articles.curatorNote: Realism is a promise to time. The face you carve today must still be that face in twenty years.

articles.title: Black as Structure
articles.paperTitle: Black as Structure: Blackwork, Dotwork, Geometry, Ornament, Blackout, and Black-and-Grey
articles.dek: Blackwork, dotwork, geometry, ornament, and blackout — where black ink becomes architecture.
articles.curatorNote: Black is not the absence of color. On skin it is structure, gravity, and the longest-lasting truth we own.

articles.title: Living Lineages: Indigenous & Heritage Systems
articles.paperTitle: Living Lineages: Indigenous and Heritage Tattoo Systems, Colonial Disruption, Revival, and Cultural Authority
articles.dek: Māori, Sāmoan, Marquesan, Haida, Celtic, and Mesoamerican marks — and why 'tribal' is not one thing.
articles.curatorNote: Some marks ask for consent and lineage I cannot grant here. This paper teaches the difference between honoring and taking.

articles.title: The Japanese Tattoo Continuum
articles.paperTitle: The Japanese Tattoo Continuum: Irezumi, Tebori, Neo-Japanese, and Anime/Manga Translation
articles.dek: Irezumi, tebori, neo-Japanese, and anime — from Edo penal marks to global fandom.
articles.curatorNote: Tebori taught me patience. A body-suit is a river of myth; you do not rush a river.

articles.title: Paper, Canvas & Screen, Translated to Skin
articles.paperTitle: Paper, Canvas, and Screen Translated to Skin: Illustrative Tattoo Languages
articles.dek: Etching, sketch, watercolor, abstraction, and Pop Art — marks born in other media, rebuilt in dermis.
articles.curatorNote: A brushstroke is not a needle. This is the art of translation — and of what survives the crossing.

articles.title: The Experimental Body
articles.paperTitle: The Experimental Body: Late-Modern, Post-Digital, Hybrid, and Anti-Canonical Tattoo Styles
articles.dek: Trash Polka, biomechanical, cyber sigilism, embroidery, glitch — post-digital, anti-canonical styles.
articles.curatorNote: The newest dialects of ink are being named as we speak. Here is where the future keeps arriving.

articles.title: Economy of the Line & the Urban Letter
articles.paperTitle: Economy of the Line and the Urban Letter: Fine-Line, Minimalism, Lettering, Chicano, and Graffiti
articles.dek: Fine-line, minimalism, single-line, lettering, Chicano, and graffiti — reduction and the street.
articles.curatorNote: Paris showed me elegance is subtraction. But the thinnest line pays the highest tax to time — know that before you choose it.

articles.title: Darkness, Devotion & the Sublime
articles.paperTitle: Darkness, Devotion, and the Sublime: Horror, Occult, Gothic, and Religious Tattooing
articles.dek: Horror, occult, gothic, and religious tattooing — fear, mortality, and the sacred on skin.
articles.curatorNote: The dark and the devotional are closer than people think. Both are ways of holding what frightens us.

articles.title: Functional & Material Exceptions
articles.paperTitle: Functional and Material Exceptions: UV, White Ink, Negative Space, Silhouette, Handpoke, and Paramedical Tattooing
articles.dek: UV, white ink, negative space, silhouette, handpoke, and paramedical work — styles defined by material, not motif.
articles.curatorNote: Some of these are art, some are healing, some are risk. I will always tell you honestly which is which.

articles.title: The Constructed Line
articles.paperTitle: The Constructed Line: Needle Grouping, Motion, Pressure, and Seven Linework Systems
articles.dek: Seven linework systems — needle grouping, motion, pressure — and why bold holds and fine fades.
articles.curatorNote: A line has a lifespan the moment it enters skin. This is how we choose it with the future in mind.

articles.title: Building Value in Skin
articles.paperTitle: Building Value in Skin: Seven Shading Systems from Soft Gradients to Crosshatching
articles.dek: Seven shading systems, from soft gradients to crosshatching — how tone is built and how it heals.
articles.curatorNote: Shadow is where a tattoo breathes. Point by point, pass by pass, we teach the skin to hold light.

articles.title: Chromatic Practice
articles.paperTitle: Chromatic Practice: Packing, Shading, Blending, Highlights, White Ink, and Watercolor Effects
articles.dek: Packing, shading, blending, highlights, white, and watercolor — how color lives, and fades, in skin.
articles.curatorNote: Color in Brazil laughs louder — but every hue negotiates with the skin beneath it. This is that negotiation.

articles.title: Point by Point
articles.paperTitle: Point by Point: Dotwork, Stippling, and Dot-Gradient Construction
articles.dek: Dotwork, stippling, and dot-gradients — three related systems built from single points of contact.
articles.curatorNote: Dotwork is meditation. Point by point, breath by breath, a shadow assembles itself.

articles.title: Constructing Illusion
articles.paperTitle: Constructing Illusion: Realistic Rendering, Depth Effects, and Optical Tattoo Techniques
articles.dek: Realistic rendering, depth effects, and optical technique — and the gap between fresh impact and durable read.
articles.curatorNote: Illusion is honest work when it respects the body's curve. Here is how depth is made without lying to the skin.

articles.title: Before & Beyond the Machine
articles.paperTitle: Before and Beyond the Machine: Hand Poke, Tebori, Hand-Tapped Tatau, and Skin Stitching
articles.dek: Hand poke, tebori, hand-tapped tatau, and skin stitching — living manual technologies, never interchangeable.
articles.curatorNote: The hand knows things the machine forgets. But these methods carry authority and lineage — respect that, or leave them alone.

articles.title: Black, Skin & Precision
articles.paperTitle: Black, Skin, and Precision: Large Fill, Negative Space, Geometry, Silhouette, and Tribal Blackfill
articles.dek: Large fill, negative space, geometry, silhouette, and tribal blackfill — precision at the scale of the whole limb.
articles.curatorNote: At this scale the skin itself becomes the drawing tool. Negative space is a decision, not a leftover.

articles.title: Simulated Media & Special Effects
articles.paperTitle: Simulated Media and Special Effects: Brush, Etching, UV, Smoke, and Fire
articles.dek: Brush, etching, UV, smoke, and fire — how texture and atmosphere are built, and where safety ends the fun.
articles.curatorNote: Effects dazzle in the chair. I will always weigh the spectacle against what your skin must carry for decades.

articles.title: Drawing with the Body
articles.paperTitle: Drawing with the Body: Freehand Composition and Layered Execution
articles.dek: Freehand composition and layered execution — designing directly on anatomy, across many sittings.
articles.curatorNote: The best compositions are drawn on the body, not on paper. The body tells you where the line wants to go.

articles.title: Working with Existing Ink
articles.paperTitle: Working with Existing Ink: Cover-Up and Blast-Over as Remedial Design Systems
articles.dek: Cover-up and blast-over — concealment versus deliberate coexistence, and the honesty to refuse.
articles.curatorNote: Old ink is a fact, not an enemy. Sometimes we hide it; sometimes we let it live beneath the new. Sometimes I say no.

articles.title: Reading Marks That Rarely Survive
articles.paperTitle: Reading Marks That Rarely Survive: Methods and Limits in the Archaeology of Tattooing
articles.dek: The archaeology of tattooing — evidence classes, imaging, and the discipline of not overclaiming.
articles.curatorNote: History humbles us. What survives is chance; what it meant is often a question we must leave open.

articles.title: Ancient Tattooing as Multiple Histories
articles.paperTitle: Ancient Tattooing as Multiple Histories: Europe, North Africa, Eurasia, the Americas, Arctic Regions, and Asia
articles.dek: Europe, North Africa, Eurasia, the Americas, and the Arctic — many origins, no single birthplace.
articles.curatorNote: There is no first tattoo, only the first that survived. The body has always wanted to speak.

articles.title: Pacific Tattoo Knowledge Systems
articles.paperTitle: Pacific Tattoo Knowledge Systems: Continuity, Genealogy, Service, Rank, Gender, and Revival
articles.dek: Sāmoan tatau, Māori tā moko, and Marquesan marks as distinct systems of genealogy, rank, and revival.
articles.curatorNote: In the Pacific, a tattoo is a genealogy you wear. It is given by authority, not bought.

articles.title: Tattooing in Japan, from Edo to Now
articles.paperTitle: Tattooing in Japan from Edo Visual Culture to Contemporary Practice
articles.dek: Woodblock imagery, body-suit composition, criminalization, and the long shadow of stigma.
articles.curatorNote: Japan taught the body-suit, and taught me patience. It also carries a stigma the West rarely sees.

articles.title: Encounter, Naming & Colonial Power
articles.paperTitle: Encounter, Naming, Collecting, and Colonial Power in the Global Tattoo Archive
articles.dek: How the word 'tattoo' traveled, and how colonial collecting shaped — and distorted — the global archive.
articles.curatorNote: Even the word we use is a souvenir of encounter. Knowing that changes how we hold the whole story.

articles.title: Electricity, Flash & the Professional Studio
articles.paperTitle: Electricity, Flash, and the Professional Tattoo Studio, 1870–1950
articles.dek: The machine patent, flash sheets, port networks, and the birth of the commercial tattoo shop, 1870–1950.
articles.curatorNote: The machine made the trade fast and cheap — and a whole profession grew around fifty punctures a second.

articles.title: Subculture & Counterpublic
articles.paperTitle: Subculture and Counterpublic: Tattooing in Military, Prison, Chicano, Biker, Punk, Queer, and Feminist Histories
articles.dek: Military, prison, Chicano, biker, punk, queer, and feminist histories — marks of belonging and resistance.
articles.curatorNote: Ink has always drawn a line between us and them. Who wears it, and who is policed for it, is never neutral.

articles.title: From Revival to Platform Culture
articles.paperTitle: From Revival to Platform Culture: Globalization, Conventions, Social Media, and Hybrid Styles
articles.dek: Conventions, artist mobility, and social media — how microstyles are named, copied, and spread overnight.
articles.curatorNote: The feed names a new style each month. Speed is exciting, but authorship and origin still deserve our care.

articles.title: The Marked Body
articles.paperTitle: The Marked Body: Identity, Ritual, Power, Stigma, Memory, and Self-Authorship
articles.dek: Identity, ritual, power, stigma, memory, and self-authorship — the framework behind all four lenses.
articles.curatorNote: Every mark does one of a few things: it protects, remembers, releases, or declares. This is the map I read by.

articles.title: Material & Governed Skin
articles.paperTitle: Material and Governed Skin: Pigments, Hygiene, Regulation, Medicine, Cosmetics, and Risk
articles.dek: Pigments, hygiene, regulation, and risk — the public-health history of putting color under skin.
articles.curatorNote: Ritual begins with a clean space. What we inject, and how we heal, is where art meets responsibility.
